newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay sugar prices extend gains on fresh buying.
newsitem.headline: Bombay sugar prices extend gains on fresh buying.

text.p: Bombay sugar prices on Thursday extended gains on fresh consumer buying and limited arrivals, dealers said.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by eight rupees at 1,438/1,465 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 moved up by 5/10 rupees at 1,475/1,510 rupees per quintal.

Sugar mill delivery rose by five rupees at 1,365/1,375 rupees per quintal for the sugar from production year 1995/96 while sugar mill delivery from production year 1996/97 was quoted higher at 1,375/1,390 rupees per quintal, dealers said.
Local millers are witnessing higher outstation buying at the mill level which in turn has cut sugar arrivals from mills to the Bombay market.
Out of the free sale quota of 800,000 tonnes for June, the government had allotted only 23,66,029 quintal of sugar to Maharashtra state while it was 26,11,305 quintal last month.
"The limited allotment for local mills out of the total free sale quota also dragged local prices upward since the commencement of the current month," one broker said.
